items.title: 68088_Wilbur B. Ware, Sr oral history interview
items.q: Burt was sounding like Benny Carter would sound... they take a fella like Benny Carter. Collins. He could play trumpet as well as alto.

ctx.x: Martha Davis, yeah. An alto player came through there out of St. Louis named Burt Brazier. Now Burt come through Chicago with a pianist -- only had one leg, Greer? and a drummer was named Sonny Greer; they were all out of St. Louis. Swinging little cats. And I mean they were older than I was. I was just, like I said, just a teenager. And they were playing, oh, to me -- Burt was sounding like Benny Carter would sound, you know, on alto. But he didn't know the music. I didn't find this out until later, because I…

the WPA band -- he was in the WPA band. He remembered me. And I said, 'Burt?' And he said, 'Bubble ...' -- he used to call everybody 'Bubble Kitchen'. He said, 'Bubble Kitchen, I never learned how to read music. I can hardly play it unless it's written out.' And I took that advice and I figured if I learned how to read, I would lose all my natural ability.

items.title: 68088_Wilbur B. Ware, Sr oral history interview
items.q: Betty 'Bebop' Benny Carter, and ... the fellow who wrote 'Two Years of Torture' -- oh God, a beautiful cat, Jimmy Witherspoon used to come, too.

ctx.x: She said, 'No sticks ... brushes.' Wam, Wam, she Naturally, wouldn't fired me and him. Now she had to get rid of the piano player. But that was the first time I worked with her. And then I had to pay my dues. Drugs caused me to go to the House of Correction in Chicago, and I spent all of 1952 in there.

When I came out, I was clean -- '53, Ike Morris Hyte has just preceeded me, he left -- that was just before he died. I was in there, he carved up some sticks and sent them down to my cell and he said to keep practicing, you know, keep your wrists up, and I did. And when I come out, I got a job at a place called the Flame -- that was on Oakwood Blav., working and a trumpet player -- a trumpet and violinist -- Melvin Porter Kilbert, Moore and alto was Killman, Earl Phillips was on drums, and Jimmy Boyle was playing…
